svg.title: Hash Table Collision Resolution: Separate Chaining vs Open Addressing Probing
svg.desc: Animated 4-panel comparison of Separate Chaining, Linear Probing showing primary clustering and tombstone markers, Quadratic Probing showing secondary clustering, and Double Hashing achieving O(m^2) distinct probe sequences.
svg.text: Collision Resolution: Separate Chaining vs Open Addressing (m = 7)
Comparing pointer chains against Linear Probing, Quadratic Probing, and Double Hashing when inserting colliding key k_new (h'(k_new) = 2)
1. Separate Chaining (α = n / m can exceed 1.0)
• Unsuccessful lookup: Θ(1 + α) · Successful: Θ(1 + α/2) under SUHA.
• Worst-case chain O(n): Java HashMap treeifies chains > 8 into Red-Black
trees (O(log n)). Pointer-chasing hurts cache locality vs open addressing.
2. Linear Probing: h(k, i) = (h'(k) + i) mod m
• Pro: Sequential slots fit in a single 64-byte L1 cache line.
• Con (Primary Clustering): Occupied run of length L absorbs new hits
with probability proportional to L+1, growing super-linearly as α → 1.
• Deletion MUST write TOMBSTONE (not null): search skips TOMB;
clearing to null would falsely break lookup for david @ T[4]!
Insert reuses TOMBSTONE slots; rehash compacts tombstones away.
3. Quadratic Probing: h(k, i) = (h'(k) + i^2) mod 7
• Avoids contiguous primary clusters by stepping quadratically (+1, +4, +9).
• Secondary Clustering: any keys with identical h'(k1) = h'(k2) trace the
EXACT same probe sequence (m linear chains instead of m^2).
• Prime m + α < 0.5 guarantees first ⌊m/2⌋ probes are distinct.
• Power-of-2 tables use triangular numbers: i(i+1)/2 mod 2^k visits all slots.
4. Double Hashing: h(k, i) = (h_1(k) + i · h_2(k)) mod 7
• Step size depends on key k, separating probe paths even when h_1 collides.
• Prime m: choose h_2(k) = 1 + (k mod (m - 1)) ∈ [1, m - 1] (coprime!).
• Power-of-2 m: choose h_2(k) always ODD (e.g., 2k + 1) ⇒ gcd(h_2, 2^r) = 1.
• Eliminates both primary and secondary clustering, closely matching
uniform hashing: expected probes ≈ 1/(1 - α) unsuccessful, ln(1/(1-α))/α hit.
